attractions.name: Awana Kancha Living Museum
attractions.description: Cultural centre preserving Andean weaving and native camelids (alpacas, llamas, vicuñas, guanacos), with demonstrations of weaving using natural dyes.

attractions.name: Pisaq Market (Mercado de artesanías)
attractions.description: Traditional artisan market selling alpaca textiles, hand-painted ceramics, silver jewellery, ponchos and handicrafts.

attractions.name: Ollantaytambo Archaeological Site
attractions.description: Inca fortress and one of the best surviving examples of Inca urban planning, with massive terraces and carved temples; the town remains inhabited.

attractions.name: Pisaq Market
attractions.description: Market stop en route between Cusco and the Sacred Valley
attractions._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

attractions.name: Awana Kancha
attractions.description: Breeding center of South American camels (guanacos, llamas, alpacas and vicunas), where artisans demonstrate ancient Andean weaving and dyeing techniques from 12 communities
attractions._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

attractions.name: Maras Salt Mines
attractions.description: Salt mines where salt has been extracted since Inca times using the same method; intense white shines like snow on a sunny day
attractions._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

attractions.name: Moray
attractions.description: Circular terraces among the hills resembling a Greek amphitheater, used as an open-air agricultural lab for adapting crops to different environmental conditions
attractions._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

attractions.name: Ollantaytambo Fortress
attractions.description: Fortress with the Temple of the Sun (six gigantic monoliths weighing over 50 tons) and the Terrace of the Ten Niches
attractions._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

attractions.name: Sacred Valley Zipline
attractions.description: Zipline over the Sacred Valley for all ages: attach a double-carabineer system to the steel lifeline, climb a 300m iron ladder and descend with a 100m rappel

local_dishes.name: Pachamanca
local_dishes.description: Ancient Andean cooking method where meats, potatoes, vegetables and herbs are slow-cooked underground with heated stones.

safety_tips.tip: Stay hydrated and avoid strenuous activity on the first day at altitude

connectivity_tips.tip: Mobile coverage is excellent in Lima, Cusco and the Sacred Valley

transport_options.description: Scenic PeruRail train with panoramic windows from Ollantaytambo to Machu Picchu Pueblo, about 1½ hours.
transport_options.how_to_use: Arrive at the station 30–40 minutes before departure. Luggage allowed per passenger: 1 backpack up to 8 kg, or 1 piece of hand luggage up to 12 kg with maximum dimensions of 115 cm (length + width + height). Larger luggage can be stored at Ollantaytambo Station.
transport_options.covers: Ollantaytambo to Machu Picchu Pueblo and return

health_tips.tip: Cusco sits at 3,400 m (11,150 ft); allow time to acclimatise and keep the first day relaxed
Coca tea, commonly offered by hotels, is a traditional remedy for altitude adjustment
UV index is very high in the Andes even on cool days; wear sunscreen, sunglasses and a hat
Walk slowly and take your time at altitude
Take it easy for the first 24-48 hours at high altitude and avoid strenuous activity, heavy meals and alcohol
health_tips._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

health_tips.tip: Coca tea (mate de coca) can help alleviate altitude symptoms; chewing coca leaves is also traditional
health_tips._source_file: South America/All Inclusive Guide - Peru- Neha and Mayur.pdf

health_tips.tip: Drink plenty of bottled water to help with altitude sickness
